arguments.summary: A critical APT activity alert was triggered by suspicious behavior originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.14), attributed to user CORP\jsmith in the Finance department. Investigation revealed a multi-stage attack chain beginning with a phishing email (simulated via Outlook) leading to execution of encoded PowerShell, loading of an unsigned DLL via rundll32 from the Temp directory, and establishment of a Cobalt Strike beacon to external C2 infrastructure (198.51.100.23:443). The host exhibited lateral movement attempts via SMB to 10.0.3.10 and failed Kerberos authentication, indicating credential testing. Despite detection by IDS, initial EDR and sandboxing tools failed to classify the activity as malicious due to obfuscation and potential rule gaps. The host was isolated via firewall block, but no malware was detected during post-isolation scanning, suggesting fileless or memory-resident techniques. The initial file 'chrome_helper.exe' (hash: f0e1...f0e1) was incorrectly marked as clean by sandbox analysis, highlighting a critical detection gap.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dynamic_DNS {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beaconing via dynamic DNS domains"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $beacon_get = "GET / HTTP/1.1" wide ascii
        $beacon_host = "Host: " wide ascii
        $dynamic_tld = ".ddns.net" wide ascii nocase
        $dynamic_tld2 = ".hopto.org" wide ascii nocase
    condition:
        all of ($beacon_*) and any of ($dynamic_tld*)
}
